complexity.correctness_reason: Both decode and encode recurse once per digit, so any list longer than CPython's recursion limit (~1000 frames) raises RecursionError — fine under the 100-node cap, broken once it is lifted.
complexity.notes: Because decode/encode operate on whole n-digit integers, the multiplications and divisions by 10 at each recursion level touch O(n) machine words, so the total work is O(n^2) word operations rather than the O(n) of per-digit arithmetic. A linear approach exists: ||walk both lists in parallel, adding digit pairs with a running carry and appending result nodes||. The `or ListNode(0)` trick is neat but slightly obscure — it depends on encode returning None exactly when n == 0, which a comment or the previous explicit conditional made clearer. Recursion depth is O(n), so the cap is doing real work here.
complexity.summary: Recursively decodes each list into a single integer (least-significant digit first), adds them, and recursively re-encodes the sum into a linked list, with `or ListNode(0)` covering the zero-sum case where encode returns None.
